bullets.title: MSFT + META: Key after-hours earnings catalysts; capex peak fears weigh pre-print
bullets.body: Microsoft and Meta both reporting after-hours; all eyes on Azure growth trajectory (record pace per Barchart) and forward capex guidance. One analyst warns 'recipe for the apocalypse' includes Meta/Microsoft signaling peak capex alongside a rate hike. Disney reportedly switching from GitHub Copilot to OpenAI Codex, a potential enterprise AI revenue headwind for MSFT.

bullets.title: META: Analyst bullish on Q2 revenue/profits; Zuck signals AI acceleration push
bullets.body: One buy-side analyst expects a strong META quarter driven by LLM-era app ecosystem advantages and Google Search share losses to social channels. Zuckerberg publicly called for US AI acceleration. Analyst also flagged AI capex will be more FCF-dilutive than chip-centric models imply. META pullback seen as a buy opportunity by at least one trader.

bullets.title: VRT: Shares drop 15% premarket on Q2 sales miss; supply chain cited
bullets.body: Vertiv reported Q2 net sales and organic growth below consensus; shares fell ~15% in premarket. Morgan Stanley cited supply chain constraints. Separately, VRT's earnings call read-throughs confirm durable, broad-based AI data-center infrastructure demand with liquid cooling expanding TAM.

bullets.title: Semis sector: Record selling, bear market, -28-29% from June peak
bullets.body: Goldman traders reported record selling and 'violent derisking' in semis. SOX is down ~28-29% in 26 trading days since June 22 peak—mirroring dot-com crash pace. Long semis was BofA's most crowded trade in July; SOXL 3x ETF down 69%. BofA clients bought the dip, but JPMorgan warns broader index selling may follow.

bullets.title: NVDA: $240M dark pool print; CDS hits all-time high signaling credit stress
bullets.body: A $240M dark pool transaction printed in NVDA. Separately, NVDA CDS hit an all-time peak, with bond markets flashing warning signals on debt despite equity price resilience. One long-term bull (CRAVE Thesis) remains incrementally more bullish post-20+ earnings calls but acknowledges stocks are not cooperating.

bullets.title: MU: Down 41% from highs; forward P/E at 5.4x vs 6.5x LT avg — fear priced in
bullets.body: MU has fallen 41% from its highs and now trades at 5.37x forward P/E versus a long-term average of 6.52x (vs. 12.6x in November). Analysts suggest significant fear is already priced in and AI bottleneck stocks may be stabilizing. Memory trade momentum questioned as potential inflection approached.

bullets.title: SNDK: Down 56-57% from ATH, hits most oversold level in 15 months
bullets.body: SanDisk plunged to a 3-month low, off 56.6% from its all-time high and at the most oversold RSI level in 15 months. A similar technical setup in April 2025 preceded a massive rally, though prior investors who bought above $2,000/share face deep losses.

bullets.title: LITE: CHIPS Act silicon photonics tailwind + IR meeting notes published
bullets.body: US government is taking a 1% stake in GlobalFoundries and awarding $300M under CHIPS Act specifically targeting CPO and silicon photonics—analysts flag LITE as a direct beneficiary. Separately, Aurelon Research published meeting notes from LITE's VP of IR plus third-party device engineer commentary. AAOI also hit by AI deleveraging with skepticism around $5.6B 2027 revenue projections vs. $6.3B market cap.

bullets.title: CRWV: Down 67% from ATH, lowest weekly RSI in history; CDS at 850bps
bullets.body: CoreWeave has fallen 67% from its all-time high and is printing its lowest weekly RSI ever, having bounced from this level three prior times. CRWV CDS are trading around 850bps, used as a proxy benchmark for where OpenAI credit would price.

bullets.title: CRM: +25% since June 22 vs. semis -29% — software divergence widens
bullets.body: Salesforce is up 25% since June 22 while the semiconductor index (SOXX) is down 29%, the starkest sector divergence of the month. AI momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) is down 37% on the month and failed to stabilize despite the largest 3-day de-gross on Goldman Prime records since November 2022.

bullets.title: ARM: 4x CPU core efficiency for agentic AI workloads positions for share gains
bullets.body: ARM claims its architecture delivers 120M CPU cores per gigawatt for agentic AI versus 30M previously—a 4x improvement—positioning competitively in power-constrained data center deployments ahead of its earnings report today.

bullets.title: AMAT / semiconductor equipment: WFE could exceed $230B in 2028; capacity doubling
bullets.body: Street models 2028 WFE at $190-200B but Top-5 equipment makers expanding aggressively—AMAT can double output with existing floor space, Lam nearly doubled capacity in 4 years, TEL targets 1.8x by FY2029, ASML turned pre-emptive post-2Q26. Price increases flowing 100% to toolmaker gross margins; suppliers like Ichor (8-17% GM) and Ultra Clean (11-21% GM) lack pricing power.

bullets.title: GLW: Worst single-day drop in 24 years on optical fiber capacity ceiling concerns
bullets.body: Corning posted its worst single-day decline in 24 years driven by optical fiber capacity ceiling concerns—a notable negative read-through for fiber infrastructure demand trajectory.

bullets.title: STX: Third consecutive 'triple play'; stock up 5%+ on earnings
bullets.body: Seagate reported its third straight quarter of beating on revenue, EPS, and guidance—shares rose over 5% following results.

bullets.title: QCOM: Earnings today; AI pivot gaining momentum amid chip sector weakness
bullets.body: Qualcomm reports earnings today. Chip stocks are off their highs but QCOM's AI pivot is cited as a positive catalyst. BMW also selected Qualcomm as lead silicon provider for its digital cockpit, though this was framed as a non-universe note.

bullets.title: TSLA: Breaks below $300, exits $1T+ market cap club
bullets.body: Tesla broke below $300 per share, dropping out of the $1 trillion market cap club. UBER continues to outperform TSLA; at least two analysts argue TSLA bulls' thesis on autonomous displacement of UBER has been wrong while UBER's autonomous partner network keeps expanding.

bullets.title: T (AT&T): Internet Air reaches 2M customers, doubling subs in roughly half the time
bullets.body: AT&T's Internet Air fixed-wireless product reached 2 million customers, doubling its subscriber base in approximately half the time it took to reach the prior milestone—accelerating growth trajectory.

bullets.title: RDDT: LightShed says Meta or X will bid for Reddit data if Google/Gemini walks
bullets.body: LightShed analysts argue Reddit has valuable AI training data and that if Google/Gemini doesn't pay for access, Meta or Elon Musk's X will compete for the rights, underpinning Reddit's data monetization floor.

bullets.title: DASH: Launches internal drone delivery division with proprietary aircraft
bullets.body: DoorDash is building a drone delivery business including its own aircraft, led by its robotics and autonomy team—a potential new growth vector beyond food delivery.

bullets.title: HIMS: FTC reportedly suing over billing, cancellation, and privacy practices
bullets.body: The FTC is reportedly suing Hims & Hers over alleged billing violations, improper cancellation practices, and privacy violations—a material regulatory risk overhang for the stock.
